items.title: [FDD Diary #10] Running Everything by Hand
content:
Yesterday the AI built it in Python.
Today, same project. TypeScript.

'Yesterday was Python.'
'Yes. Python was more suitable yesterday.'

Same project. Different language. Every day.

'Build the agent system.'
AI dumped a thousand lines. Ran it. Blew up.
No idea where.

Two things missing between spec and code.
Tech decisions. Task breakdown.

I had the 'what.'
Didn't have the 'how' or the 'in what order.'

Wrote it down before throwing it at the AI.
'TypeScript. Rust runtime. Existing transport module.'

Python stopped showing up.

Broke the big thing into small pieces.
One piece breaks? Fix that piece. Rest stays.

Specify. Plan. Tasks. Implement.
Four steps.

items.title: [FDD Diary #11] Words Evaporate
content:
Made one file. Named it CLAUDE.md.
Put three rules in it.
The AI read it automatically.

Next morning, everything was different.

Before CLAUDE.md:
'Build this.' AI starts from scratch.
'Read the spec first.' Every time. By hand.

After CLAUDE.md:
'Build this.' AI checks the spec.
Asks about what's missing.
Follows the plan.

Same AI. Different environment.

Words evaporate.
Environment stays.

No matter how good your prompts are.
One well-placed file beats them all.

Not 'I told the AI what to do.'
'The environment tells the AI what to do.'

That's the difference between a prompt and a system.

items.title: [FDD Diary #12] The Loop Clicks
content:
Same feature. Forty-five minutes.
Used to take a week.

Not because I got better.
Because PROBLEMS.md existed.
Because SSOT existed.
Because the AI stopped guessing.

Error rate dropped. 40% to 5%.
Code stopped colliding.
AI checks existing code before building.

Wrote rules in CLAUDE.md.
'No coding without decisions. Spec first.'

The AI changed.
Stopped building from scratch.
A system was running.

But the code kept growing.
Five thousand lines. Ten thousand. Twenty thousand.

Opened the user settings screen.
Agent status was showing there.

Why is this here?
